name: kimi-memory
description: Three-layer local memory for Kimi Code (global user memory, per-project durable + working memory, per-project session archives) plus an integrated advisor subsystem for reflective prompts. Exposed via MCP tools, lifecycle hooks, and slash commands.
skillInstructions: Use the kimi-memory MCP tools. Routing rules: (1) durable facts about the user, their environment, or reusable workflows are GLOBAL — pass scope:'global' on memory_save so they land in $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/_global/memory.sqlite. (2) Durable facts about the active project (repo conventions, decisions, architectures) are PROJECT — default scope for memory_save/update/delete. (3) Transient current focus is working_memory_set/get/clear (project-only). (4) Session transcripts are conversation_list/get/search/ingest (project-only, automatic). memory_recall/list/get default to scope:'all' so a default caller sees project + global hits; pass scope:'project' or scope:'global' to filter. memory_similar and memory_conclusions_for also accept scope:'all' (project first, then global). Always pass `cwd` (the active project root), even for global writes — it stays as provenance context. Prefer memory_recall (scope:'all') before memory_save to avoid duplicates; if a recall hit exists, update or use supersede:true instead of saving a second copy. Use memory_link to write a typed edge between related memories, memory_merge to synthesize several rows into one, and memory_save with type:'conclusion' + synthesizes:[childIds] to record a higher-order synthesis. Use memory_reinforce after reading a recall hit so it stays fresh against decay. Echo the returned operation, scope, and id so the user can see what was persisted. Never store secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords, credentials, .env contents, PII). Advisor subsystem: when the UserPromptSubmit hook emits `[advisor] matched: "..."`, the prompt matched a reflection keyword — load skill `advisor` (or invoke /advisor) and follow the anchored-recommendation procedure. Do NOT push changes without the user's go-ahead. The advisor skill is loaded on demand; memory skill is loaded at SessionStart.

interface.shortDescription: Three-layer local memory plus a reflective advisor layer, exposed via MCP tools, lifecycle hooks, and slash commands.
interface.longDescription: Single plugin that merges the previous kimi-memory + kimi-advisor plugins. Two subsystems: (1) Memory — a kimi-memory MCP server with three storage layers: GLOBAL durable memory at $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/_global/memory.sqlite for cross-project user preferences and reusable workflows; PROJECT durable + working memory at $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/<project-key>/memory.sqlite for repository facts and current focus; and PROJECT session archives (conversations and conversation_events) ingested idempotently from Kimi's wire.jsonl; SHARED cross-project pool at $KIMI_CODE_HOME/kimi-memory/_shared/memory.sqlite (project_key='_shared') holds ACL-promoted rows that should be visible across projects. Tools (46): durable memory — memory_save (now also accepts visibility + shared_with + team_id/agent_id/user_id/session_id/task_id), memory_recall (RRF-fused hybrid FTS5 + embedding cosine by default; `fusion: 'weighted'` preserves the legacy 0.5/0.5 blend for one release; rrf_k overrides the default RRF_K=60; optional visibility filter), memory_list, memory_get, memory_update (same v10 ACL fields), memory_delete, memory_save_bulk (atomic 1–500 with all-or-nothing rollback, supports type=conclusion + synthesizes[] + type=skill + per-item ACL fields); similarity + graph — memory_similar, memory_link, memory_unlink, memory_edges, memory_merge; synthesis — memory_conclusions_for, memory_parents; importance — memory_reinforce; ACL / visibility (v10) — acl_grant (insert into memories_acl), acl_revoke, acl_list, acl_share_memory (in-place promotion OR move into the _shared pool), acl_resolve_principal (parse 'kind:id'); tier / persona (v10) — memory_set_tier (explicit L0→L1→L2→L3 move + audit row), memory_promote / memory_demote (one-step up/down), memory_tier_history (audit log); wiki / LLM-Wiki (v10) — wiki_upsert_page (idempotent on (project, name); parses [[wiki-name]] + [text](wiki:name) body markers when no explicit links supplied), wiki_get_page (by id or name), wiki_traverse (BFS graph walk), wiki_backlinks (incoming edges), wiki_resolve (name → page record); codegraph (v10) — codegraph_extract (walk a project; extract function/class/const + import lines from .js/.ts/.py; skips node_modules), codegraph_build_edges (write calls|imports|defines edges into memory_edges between memories that share symbols; dry-run by default), codegraph_query_symbol (BFS over the memory graph), codegraph_impact_path (shortest path via codegraph edges), codegraph_callers, codegraph_callees; maintenance — memory_prune (orphan-project cleanup, dry-run-first), memory_reset_project (wipe a single project's per-project rows after a repo is re-cloned to the same canonical path; the project_key is a hash of the path so a re-clone is otherwise indistinguishable from the original); working_memory_set/get/clear (project-only); conversation_list/get/search/ingest (project-only); memory_status (combined project + global summary, with a re-clone diagnostic). Schema v10: v6 project_paths, v7 last_embed_error, v8 last_canonical_root + record_count, v9 stability_days + last_rehearsed_at (Ebbinghaus decay), v10 visibility (private|team|restricted|agent|task) + shared_with + 5 nullable principal identity columns + memories_acl table for explicit grants. saveMemory runs a persist-layer secret check (KIMI_MEMORY_SECRET_DETECTED on title or content matching a known credential shape); the only opt-out is KIMI_MEMORY_SECRET_SCAN=off. The encoder load is wall-clock bounded (4s default, KIMI_MEMORY_EMBED_TIMEOUT_MS) so a slow model download cannot block the hook. v0.5.1: src/auto-gc.js runs three independent fail-open passes on every SessionStart (auto-prune of dead/superseded/cold/orphan rows, auto-archive of raw conversation_events/skill_invocations/persona_promotions, auto-tier promotion/demotion); tier promotion runs every open, prune+archive are throttled to once per 6h per project via schema_meta(auto_gc_last_run). The consolidate pass also auto-merges tight clusters (cosine >= 0.85, tag overlap >= 2, >= 3 members) by folding siblings into the highest-confidence member via memory_merge (soft-supersede, never hard-delete). The persistence layer was split into focused modules under src/persist/ (connection, memories, search, reinforce, edges, share, skills, project, re-exports) with src/persist.js kept as a backward-compatibility barrel. UserPromptSubmit now writes a trailing JSON object on stdout with systemMessage + hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext so per-memory recall lines reach the model without flooding the terminal. A standalone kimi-memory CLI bin entry exposes list/get/status/recall/prune/reset-project + acl list|grant|revoke for ops debugging without spinning up the MCP server. Background importance decay runs in the SessionStart hook (Ebbinghaus curve 0.1 + 0.9*exp(-days/stability), 30-day grace, floor 0.1). Auto-extraction runs in the Stop hook (and any handler that delegates to it) and writes durable candidates with provenance.source='auto_extract'; the embedding model is downloaded lazily from Hugging Face on first use, and auto-extraction sends a bounded prompt to the configured model provider — both can be disabled. The UserPromptSubmit hook emits a per-type recall summary and up to three [recall: i/N] lines with a bounded body snippet, so the user can verify the recall at a glance. (2) Advisor — fail-open UserPromptSubmit detection against a frozen keyword list (15 phrases: 'would we change', 'what would you do differently', 'second opinion', etc.) with a per-sentence negation gate (so 'I wouldn't change anything' does not fire) emits a one-line hint when matched; skill `advisor` is loaded on demand and runs the anchored-recommendation procedure (recall global + project, read live project state, output structured findings with severity/evidence/action, negative space, follow-up question). Slash commands: /kimi-memory:list_memories, /kimi-memory:advisor, /kimi-memory:prune, /kimi-memory:memos (companion dashboard).
